content.comment_body: Hello, I am working with an [product_name] input module and want to understand the scaling of a 4-20mA signal. For 0-10V signals, each volt corresponds to 100 counts, and for 0-20mA signals, each 1mA is 50 counts. How should the 4-20mA be scaled, and why is the offset set to 250 instead of 200?
Hi [user_name], please refer to the following resources for more information: [url] and [url].

Hello [user_name], 4-20mA loops can be complex. Typically, a 4-20mA signal represents the measured value; for example, a 0-100 unit measurement could result in 4mA at 0 and 20mA at 100. Scaling in the PLC depends on the input module used. To ensure correct configuration, consider using a current loop tester to validate your PLC program.

The [product_name] does not differentiate between 0-20mA and 4-20mA signals. If correctly scaled, the input will produce valid values in your program. Internally, [product_name] works with a range of 0-1000 for 0-20mA or 0-10V inputs and outputs.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for accurate methods for scaling 4-20mA analog signals, especially regarding offset values within [product_name] analog modules.
